findings.title: Import promises are created eagerly, so every app module loads at import time
findings.body: Each entry is written as `import("./x")`, which starts loading the module as soon as the object literal is evaluated. Any module that imports appStore therefore loads all ~28 app modules up front, which defeats the purpose of async loading. Wrapping each entry in an arrow, e.g. `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`, would defer loading until a caller asks for the app. Callers would then need to invoke the function instead of awaiting the property. Also, a rejected import that nobody awaits becomes an unhandled rejection.

findings.title: Async forEach callback makes the try/catch useless and drops rejections
findings.body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...)` does not await the callbacks. The `try/catch` below only catches synchronous throws, so any rejection from `getCalendar`, `deleteEvent` or `deleteMeeting` becomes an unhandled promise rejection, and the error is never logged. The function also returns `true` and sends the reschedule email before the cancellations have run. Use `for...of` with `await`, or `Promise.allSettled` over mapped promises, so failures are caught and logged.

findings.title: Async forEach callback makes the try/catch useless and drops rejections
findings.body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...)` does not await the callbacks. The `try/catch` only catches synchronous throws, so failures from `getCalendar`, `deleteEvent` or `deleteMeeting` become unhandled rejections and are never logged. The function also proceeds to send the email before the cancellations finish. Use `for...of` with `await`, or `Promise.allSettled`.

findings.title: Recurring cancellation pushes to apiDeletes after it has already been awaited
findings.body: The `forEach(async (credential) => ...)` callback awaits `getCalendar` and then pushes `deleteEvent` promises into `apiDeletes`. Nothing waits for these callbacks, and `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` runs later with the array as it was at that point. Calendar deletions for recurring bookings may therefore be skipped from the awaited set, and their rejections go unhandled. Replace this with a `for...of` loop that awaits each credential.

findings.title: Async forEach callback in requestReschedule ignores its returned promises
findings.body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => ...)` discards the promises from `getCalendar`, `deleteEvent` and `deleteMeeting`. The mutation then sends the reschedule email and resolves, while calendar and video cancellations are still running. Any rejection is unhandled and invisible to the caller. Use `for...of` with `await` or `Promise.allSettled`.

findings.title: getCalendarCredentials stores unawaited promises that can reject unhandled
findings.body: `getCalendar(credential)` is now async, but it is still called without await, and the promise is stored in the `calendar` field. If the dynamic import of an app fails, that promise rejects. The rejection is only observed later, in `getConnectedCalendars`, so Node may report it as unhandled first. Also, the `.flatMap` callback no longer produces a value that matches its old synchronous meaning.

findings.title: Video adapters are resolved one at a time instead of in parallel
findings.body: The `for...of` loop in `getVideoAdapters` awaits each `appStore` import in sequence. The dynamic imports are independent, so this serializes module loading for every video credential. `Promise.all` over the credentials would avoid the extra latency.
